# Crude MessagePack timestamp fork

Source: `github.com/tinylib/msgp` **v1.6.5**, copied from the Go module cache.
The upstream module identity, dependencies, source and license are retained.

This fork makes the default byte-slice and streaming time APIs use the standard
MessagePack timestamp extension **-1**, with the canonical timestamp-32/64/96
layout. Both explicit `TimeExt` APIs use the same implementation. Unix seconds
and nanoseconds are encoded independently, preserving the full signed 64-bit
second range without duration arithmetic. Decoding validates nanoseconds and
payload length and returns UTC; a Go zero time therefore remains canonical zero
and does not paint a different calendar date in the shell's local zone.

There is no reader for upstream's private extension 5. Extension dispatch and JSON
conversion recognize only extension -1 as a time. Generated time methods already
call these default runtime APIs, so no field-specific adapter or alternate
generator path is needed. `TimeSize` remains the 15-byte maximum size.
`NextType` recognizes an exact-length fixed extension without requiring a trailing
byte; otherwise standalone timestamp-32/64 values were not dispatched as times.

The upstream streaming writer size assertion is updated for timestamp-64. Added
timestamp regression/fuzz tests exercise both byte-slice and streaming paths.
`msgp/defgen_test.go` is the upstream test fixture generated by its documented
prepare step (`go run . -file msgp/defs_test.go -o msgp/defgen_test.go -tests=false`),
retained so the module-cache source's otherwise-missing test methods compile.
Other upstream behavior is unchanged. `internal/wiregen` includes the runtime
source bytes in the protocol schema fingerprint so primitive wire changes cannot
silently negotiate as the previous protocol.
